observation.visible_scene: A single lit candle seated in a shallow, scallop/oyster-shell-like holder with a pool of melted wax around the wick, set against a pure black background. A faint watermark text sits in the lower-right corner. The flame is the only luminous element, casting a warm glow on the wax pool and the inner rim of the holder.
visible_changes: The flame grows markedly taller and more slender over the excerpt: in the early frames it is a short, broad teardrop whose tip sits well below the upper edge, while in the later frames it stretches into a long, narrow spike reaching near the top of the image.
The flame's tip color shifts from a yellow-orange cap to a deeper, thinner reddish-orange point as it elongates.
Small frame-to-frame fluctuations in the flame's width and outline (flicker) are visible, but the overall trend is upward elongation rather than collapse.
The wick, the shell holder, the wax pool, and the watermark remain in fixed screen positions throughout; the glow on the wax stays roughly constant.
No camera translation or rotation is evident—the static holder and watermark anchor the frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the flame was already lengthening before the first sampled frame or continues to grow after the last is not shown.
The cause of the elongation (air current, wick condition, wax consumption) is not observable.
Any later outcome such as the flame shrinking, guttering, or going out is outside this segment.
uncertain_details: Any slight lateral sway of the flame is hard to confirm against the elongation and may be flicker rather than directional drift.
The exact material of the holder (shell vs. molded dish) and the wax composition cannot be determined from the images alone.
